6600.evidence: Champ cars used turbocharged engines that ran on methanol fuel. Cosworth (later branded as the Ford-Cosworth), Ilmor (branded as Chevrolet), and Buick engines were common powerplants through the mid-1990s. Mercedes-Benz took over as Ilmor's branding, while Honda and Toyota joined as factory efforts. By the 1990s, engines were typically leased from manufacturers, who conducted research and development during the racing season; one engine could easily dominate competition in the first part of the season and then fall behind. The exclusive availability of more advanced versions of engines to certain teams in the early-1990s became a major source of contention within the organization, and manufacturers fiercely resisted proposals to have engines simply be purchased by teams. In 2003, after the withdrawal of Honda and Toyota, CART purchased a series of identical 2.65L V-8 turbocharged Cosworth engines and leased them to teams under Ford branding.
